sections.h2: What should a Wayne homeowner know before selling quickly?
sections.html:
Selling a house in Wayne, New Jersey is shaped by one township rule that many sellers do not expect: a Continued Certificate of Occupancy, or CCO, that must be issued before most sales close. Add the state's closing fees and Passaic County's assessment calendar, and you have the three items that decide how fast a Wayne sale can move.

Whether you hire an agent, go it alone or sign with a cash buyer, the CCO applies, so start there.

sections.h2: Where is Wayne and what shapes its housing market?
sections.html:
Wayne spreads over 23.72 square miles of land in Passaic County, and water adds another 1.42 square miles. It touches eleven municipalities: Haledon, Little Falls, North Haledon, Pompton Lakes and Totowa in Passaic County, Franklin Lakes and Oakland in Bergen County, Fairfield and North Caldwell in Essex County, and Lincoln Park and Pequannock in Morris County. The legislature formed the township in 1847 out of Manchester Township, and its namesake is General Anthony Wayne. George Washington used the Dey Mansion as his headquarters in 1780.

Water defines many neighborhoods. Lake communities surround Packanack Lake, Pines Lake, Lions Head Lake and Tom's Lake, and half of Pompton Lake lies in Wayne. The Passaic River also crosses the township and often floods near Willowbrook Mall and the riverside neighborhoods, so ask your insurer and surveyor about flood-zone status before you list a house in those areas. Other named areas include Preakness, Mountain View, Pompton Falls, Two Bridges and Barbours Mills.

The township is a bedroom suburb of New York City, less than 20 miles from Midtown Manhattan. William Paterson University, founded in 1855, has more than 11,500 students in undergraduate and graduate programs. Willowbrook Mall holds about 200 retailers, and Valley Bank keeps its headquarters here.

sections.h2: How do highways and trains affect Wayne home values?
sections.html:
Interstate 80, U.S. Routes 46 and 202, Route 23 and county routes 502 and 504 cross the township, and the 229.48 miles of public road include 180.59 miles kept up by the municipality, 41.05 miles by Passaic County and 7.84 miles by the state. NJ Transit's Mountain View and Wayne Route 23 stations on the Montclair-Boonton Line run to Hoboken, with Midtown Direct connections to New York Penn Station. Buses reach the Port Authority Terminal on several routes.

Newark Liberty International Airport is 25.9 miles away and LaGuardia is 30 miles away. If your street is close to a station, say so in the listing.

A median owner-occupied value of $612,700 places a typical Wayne sale in the $550,000 to $850,000 bracket of the state fee chart. Gross rent has a median of $2,164, roughly one home in five is renter-occupied, and 30.0% of residents speak another language at home.

Wayne Public Schools teach pre-kindergarten through grade 12 in 15 schools, with 7,746 students enrolled in the 2022-23 school year. Wayne Hills High School serves students who live on or north of Ratzer Road, and Wayne Valley High School serves those south of it, so your street decides your high school. Elementary schools include Dey, Fallon, Kennedy, Lafayette, Packanack, Pines Lake, Ryerson, Terhune and Carter, and the three middle schools are Schuyler-Colfax, George Washington and Anthony Wayne.

Passaic County Technical Institute also admits students from across the county. Private options include DePaul Catholic High School and Al-Ghazaly High School.

sections.h2: What is a Continued Certificate of Occupancy in Wayne?
sections.html:
Wayne requires a CCO for the sale or rental of one- and two-family homes, duplexes, townhouses and condominiums. No residential premises may change ownership, tenancy or use without a CCO from the Enforcement Officer under Township Code Section 100. A transfer between spouses, from parent to child, or between siblings does not need one.

  • Apply and pay the base fee online. The Building Department then checks for open permits, and open permits must be closed before an inspection is scheduled.
  • After that, the enforcement officer has 15 business days to inspect and either issue the certificate or list the failed items.
  • Inspections sooner than 10 days after the application and permit closure carry an expediting fee.
  • A CCO is valid for 90 days. If closing slips past that, you must reapply.

The inspection checks the house against the zoning and property maintenance ordinances, including any addition, finished basement, shed, second kitchen, deck or pool, and each must have a permit or a variance. If the house fails or permits are still open, the township may allow the sale to close on a signed purchaser's agreement that names who will fix the items. That agreement cannot run longer than 60 days, and the buyer schedules the follow-up inspection.

A separate CCO fire inspection is also needed. Call the CCO Office at 973-694-1800, extension 3263, and the Fire Bureau at extension 3300. The township's CCO page links a search for open permits, so check it before you apply.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees come with a Wayne sale?
sections.html:
On the state chart for prices above $350,000, the slice from $550,000 to $850,000 costs $5.30 per $500 and the slice to $1,000,000 costs $5.80. Anything higher adds a Graduated Percent Fee that begins at 1%. Every owner files a GIT/REP form with the deed.

A New Jersey resident files GIT/REP-3. Sellers who have moved out of state file GIT/REP-1 or 2 and may prepay 2% of the price or 8.97% of the gain. The township has also warned residents about a phone scam claiming a property is in a tax sale. To confirm what you owe, call the township at 973-694-1800, extension 3330, and do not send money to a caller.

sections.h2: How do Wayne assessments and appeals work?
sections.html:
Passaic County keeps the usual calendar. Appeals are due April 1, moving to May 1 after a revaluation or reassessment. Form A-1 goes to the Passaic County Board of Taxation in Totowa (930 Riverview Drive, Suite 250; 973-720-7399). Assessments above $1,000,000 may go to the Tax Court.

The burden of proof is yours, so bring recent sales of comparable homes. Sellers rarely benefit from an appeal, but an heir or buyer keeping the house might.

sections.h2: What are the quick-sale choices in Wayne?
sections.html:
• Agent listing: broad exposure to commuters and university-area buyers, with weeks of showings and lender timelines.
  • Private sale: saves a commission, and you handle the CCO, disclosures and contracts.
  • Cash offer: no mortgage contingency, and a buyer willing to close on a purchaser's agreement if an item fails.

Whatever you choose, start the CCO early and find open permits first, since that clock controls most Wayne closing dates.

faqs.q: How long does a Wayne CCO take?
faqs.a: The enforcement officer has 15 business days to inspect and decide once the permit check is clear. Expedited inspections inside 10 days carry an extra fee, so apply as early as you can.

faqs.q: Is a CCO required when I give my house to a family member?
faqs.a: No for transfers between spouses, from parent to child, or between siblings. Other transfers of one- or two-family homes need the Continued Certificate of Occupancy.

faqs.q: How long does a Wayne CCO last?
faqs.a: Ninety days from issue. If closing has not happened by then, the certificate expires and a new application is needed.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal a property tax assessment in Wayne?
faqs.a: April 1, unless the township did a revaluation or reassessment, in which case it is May 1. File with the Passaic County Board of Taxation in Totowa at 973-720-7399.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Wayne house if it fails the CCO inspection?
faqs.a: Possibly. The township may allow closing on a purchaser's agreement that says who corrects the items, for no more than 60 days, and the buyer schedules the follow-up inspection.
